subject: Capacity MAP - GPU runway & procurement checklist
messages:
From: Mike Torres <mike.torres@acmehealth.com>
To: tessa.morgan@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@acmehealth.com
Date: Thu, 18 Apr 2024 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Capacity MAP kickoff - initial requirements

Tessa —

Thanks for the walkthrough earlier. To get the MAP formalized on our side we need a short checklist that ties evaluation milestones to the capacity commit and procurement lead times. High-level asks from the product and procurement teams:

- Private deployment (VPC) with isolation for PHI processing.
- Day-one performance target: support 3000 QPS @ 128-token average latency 99p < 220ms (inference SLO).
- Baseline capacity: equivalent of ~20 A100 GPUs for pilot, scale to ~80 A100-equiv within 6 months.
- Preferred hardware: if H100 delivers same unit economics, we are open to mix.
- Go-live target: Sept 1, 2024. Procurement needs invoice and contract stub by May 10 to start internal approvals.

Can you send a draft MAP that enumerates evaluation gates, acceptance criteria, and the procurement lead-time assumptions (rack build, cloud region scheduling, on-prem staging if needed)? Procurement is CC'd.

Thanks —
Mike
Mike Torres
Director, Platform Engineering | Acme Health

From: tessa.morgan@redwood.ai <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Mike Torres <mike.torres@acmehealth.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai, procurement@acmehealth.com
Date: Fri, 19 Apr 2024 09:38:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Capacity MAP kickoff - draft and suggested runway

Mike —

Appreciate the clarity. Attached is a concise MAP draft (MAP_draft_v1.xlsx) and a capacity sizing sheet (capacity_sizing_sheet.csv). Below is the proposed MAP condensed into milestones so procurement and engineering can align quickly.

MAP (summary) — phases and target dates (subject to final signatures):
1) Evaluation (2 weeks) — workload runs on redwood-hosted sandbox; success = 99p latency < target on synthetic and 3 production prompt families.
2) Pilot (4 weeks) — private VPC pilot with subset of traffic (canary 10% -> 25%). Acceptance = pass load+security checks, SOC2 evidence review.
3) Capacity commit (order) — upon Pilot acceptance: place reservation. Lead-time assumptions: 12–16 weeks for rack procurement & regional placement if special H100 units required; 6–8 weeks if using in-region A100 stock. We will provide a tranching plan to align hardware availability and your go-live needs.
4) Onboarding & Verification (3–4 weeks) — staging, QA, and runbook handover.

Sizing option A (staggered, lower immediate spend): 20 A100-equivalent day 1 (pilot), +30 (month 3), +30 (month 6).
Sizing option B (frontloaded, faster scale): 40 day 1 (bigger pilot), +40 (month 4).

Key asks from Acme: confirm preferred tranche model, willing-to-commit window (12/24 months), and any constraints on vendor onboarding (PO vs. direct contract).

Internal team — please review the lead-time numbers and sizing equivalencies below and flag any operational risks. I want this MAP to be a true mutual action plan with dates we can trust.

Attachments: MAP_draft_v1.xlsx, capacity_sizing_sheet.csv

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Sr. Solutions Lead | Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: tessa.morgan@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai
Cc: Mike Torres <mike.torres@acmehealth.com>, procurement@acmehealth.com
Date: Fri, 19 Apr 2024 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Capacity MAP kickoff - sizing & infra notes

Tessa / team —

Quick notes from infra on sizing and delivery risk:

- Hardware equivalency: 1 H100 (80GB) ~= 1.6 A100 (80GB) for inference throughput on our kernel set. So "20 A100-equiv" could map to ~12–13 H100s. We should show both vectors in the MAP (A100 path vs H100 path).
- Lead times: H100 chipset orders are variable. If Acme requires H100 specifically we should plan 14–18 weeks from order to rack-in-region (including cabling, NVMe staging, and smoke tests). For A100 we have shorter lanes (6–10 weeks) in major cloud regions.
- Rack & network: add 10 business days for on-site staging and security acceptance testing in a VPC/private deployment. If customer requires FIPS-compliant HSM integration, tack on another 2 weeks.
- Performance sanity checks: plan a 72-hour soak at target QPS with production payload samples during the Pilot. Include real KV cache behavior in tests (not just synthetic seqs).

Operational ask: Priyom — can you draft a simple runbook step for "order -> rack -> stage -> pilot traffic shift" with explicit dates for the 12/16/18-week scenarios?

Ben
Ben Carter
Head of Capacity Programs | Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: tessa.morgan@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai
Cc: Mike Torres <mike.torres@acmehealth.com>, procurement@acmehealth.com
Date: Sat, 20 Apr 2024 08:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Capacity MAP kickoff - procurement path & timeline

Team / Mike —

I put together a procurement-focused checklist and timeline (procurement_timeline.pdf attached). Highlights and proposed dates (assumes decision and signed SOW by May 10):

- May 10: Sign SOW & attach MAP as Annex A. (Acme procurement signoff)
- May 13: Initial deposit/invoice issued (50% of first tranche) -> triggers order to vendor.
- May 15–Jun 30: Vendor and Redwood coordinate rack allocation and hardware procurement (6–8 weeks if A100 path).
- Jul 1–Jul 14: Staging and on-site acceptance tests.
- Jul 15–Aug 5: Pilot traffic ramp and verification.
- Sep 1: Target go-live if we choose the A100 lane and keep the May 10 sign date.

Commercials: We can offer a pricing tier if Acme commits to a 12-month reservation vs. a 24-month reservation (typical uplift if shorter commit). I'll prepare two redlines for the SOW (12M & 24M).

HubSpot link to draft MAP/deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234567/deal/98765
DocuSign stub will be ready today and I will drop the link inline in the MAP.

Marissa Cole
VP, Customer Success | Redwood Inference

From: Mike Torres <mike.torres@acmehealth.com>
To: tessa.morgan@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@acmehealth.com
Date: Sat, 20 Apr 2024 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Capacity MAP kickoff - GPU runway & procurement checklist

Tessa / Marissa / Ben / Priyom —

Thanks — this is exactly the level of detail we needed. Acme can commit to the A100 path with the staggered tranche model initially (Option A). We will target the May 10 SOW sign date and 12-month reservation to start. Procurement has reviewed and will expect the invoice stub and SOW redlines by EOD Monday.

Next steps:
- Marissa: please send DocuSign link and commercial redlines (12M vs 24M) and an invoice template.
- Ben / Priyom: Priyom, please add the 12-week and 16-week timelines into the runbook and highlight the gating criteria that would force us to shift to an H100 path (supply shortage).
- Tessa: can we lock a kickoff call for Monday 4/22 10:00 PT to finalize the MAP and sign-off?

Procurement CC concurs and will prepare an internal PO flow once they see the stub.

Appreciate the fast turnaround.
Mike
